top_module.name: active_aero_controller
top_module.description: Top-level integrated controller that exposes configuration, model-service request/response interfaces, actuator command outputs, and diagnostics. It may internally instantiate a register/control wrapper, a request/response protocol engine, and a safety arbitration/datapath block, but the externally visible top module is the required integration point.
top_module.functionality: Implements the full digital contract for safe interaction with an external remote aerodynamic surrogate model service. The controller latches configuration before operation, checks geometry and flow input validity, enforces flow-envelope compliance, checks geometry format support, packs and issues one outstanding model request at a time, validates model responses by sequence and freshness, verifies required response fields, arbitrates between model-driven intent and deterministic fallback, applies clamp and optional rate limiting to each actuator command field, and exposes fault/diagnostic status. All model-service behaviors are external; only request/response handling and actuator safety control exist in RTL.
responsibilities: Latch configuration registers for model identifier, checkpoint identifier, request timeout threshold, response freshness threshold, min/max actuator command limits, command rate limit, safe fallback command value, supported geometry format selector, and control_gain or intent map selector.
Reject unsupported geometry format or out-of-envelope flow conditions and force safe fallback.
Generate exactly one outstanding request sequence at a time unless the queue depth is expanded in a future parameterization.
Transmit opaque geometry tokens and fixed-point flow conditions to the off-chip model service.
Validate response sequence and freshness, and require all fields to be present before a response can affect control.
Generate deterministic clamped fallback commands whenever a fault is present or no valid response is available.
Count accepted requests, accepted responses, rejected responses, clamp events, and fallback activations using saturating counters.
top_module.reset_behavior: On synchronous active-low reset assertion, all internal configuration latches, outstanding request tracking, sequence counters, request timestamp/cycle tags, validation flags, fault latch state, clamp state, fallback state, actuator output registers, and saturating diagnostic counters return to safe defaults. Safe defaults shall be non-actuating, with actuator_cmd_valid deasserted, actuator_cmd driven to the configured or default safe fallback command, and safe_fallback_active asserted until a fresh valid response is later accepted and all fault conditions clear.
behavior_rules: A request may be issued only when geometry_valid and flow_valid are asserted, configuration is latched, the controller is not in fault-latched fallback unless the fault has already cleared, and no previous request is outstanding.
flow_velocity_mps must be checked against the inclusive operating envelope 20..55 m/s; any out-of-envelope sample asserts envelope_violation and forces fallback.
geometry_format must match the configured supported geometry format selector; any mismatch asserts unsupported_format and forces fallback.
model_req_payload shall include model identifier, checkpoint identifier, geometry token, flow_velocity_mps, sequence number, local request timestamp or cycle tag, and validity bits.
model_req_ready shall indicate acceptance capability for an outgoing request and model_req_valid shall assert when a request is actually issued.
model_rsp_valid is only accepted when a matching outstanding request exists.
model_rsp_seq must match the outstanding sequence; any mismatch asserts stale_or_mismatched_response, increments rejected response diagnostics, and ignores all response fields.
Response freshness must be evaluated against model_rsp_timestamp or equivalent local age tag; responses older than the configured freshness threshold are stale and ignored.
Required response fields drag_force, lift_force, surface_pressure, and flow_field must be present and valid; absence of any required field asserts response_invalid and forces fallback.
Validated surrogate outputs are mapped into actuator intent through a deterministic programmable intent selector or control_gain path; no plant physics is computed in RTL.
Every actuator command field passes through clamp and optional rate limiting against configured min and max bounds; any saturation or delta limiting sets clamp_event.
safe_fallback_active remains asserted until a fresh, sequence-matched, valid response is received and the fault condition clears.
No stale, invalid, mismatched, or unsupported response may reach actuator_cmd.

actuator_cmd_valid asserts only when a command vector is available after arbitration and clamp checks; otherwise fallback command is driven and valid may remain asserted only if the design policy treats fallback as an available command.
Diagnostic counters shall saturate at all-ones and never wrap.

modules.name: active_aero_controller_cfg
modules.description: Configuration and register-latch block for control parameters, geometry support selection, reference condition record, and diagnostic readback. It provides explicit semantic configuration outputs used by the request/validation/control datapath.
modules.functionality: Implements readable and writable configuration registers that are latched before operation. The block stores model_id and checkpoint identifier, request timeout threshold, response freshness threshold, actuator command limits, command rate limit, safe fallback command, supported geometry format selector, control_gain or intent map selector, and the reference condition record for stream_velocity_mps=38.89 and geometry_format=STL with geometry_source metadata. It exposes explicit semantic outputs for use by the control engine.
responsibilities: Decode cfg_wr_en/cfg_rd_en/cfg_addr/cfg_wdata into stable configuration registers.
Provide readable cfg_rdata and cfg_ready for system software access.
Maintain latched configuration outputs that are consumed by the controller datapath.
Represent the reference condition record as digitally accessible configuration state.
modules.reset_behavior: All configuration registers and outputs reset to safe non-actuating defaults, with minimum/maximum command bounds arranged so that safe fallback is permitted, and with reference-condition outputs restored to the specified reference record defaults.
behavior_rules: Configuration outputs are latched and used by downstream control logic.
The reference condition must reflect stream_velocity_mps=38.89 and geometry_format=STL along with geometry_source metadata.
No configuration write may directly drive actuator outputs; only downstream validated control logic may do so.
Readable and writable registers must be synthesizable and synchronous.

modules.name: active_aero_controller_engine
modules.description: Protocol, validation, safety arbitration, clamping, rate limiting, fallback, and diagnostic datapath. It consumes latched configuration and external service inputs, produces model request payloads, validates responses, and generates actuator commands and fault flags.
modules.functionality: Performs request sequence generation, request packing, response sequence and freshness checking, required-field presence checking, envelope checking, unsupported-format detection, safe fallback arbitration, deterministic command intent selection, clamping, rate limiting, and saturating diagnostic counting. This block ensures that only validated, fresh, sequence-matched, and clamp-compliant commands can reach the actuator output path.
responsibilities: Track at most one outstanding request sequence and reject additional issue attempts until the prior request is resolved or timed out.
Pack model_req_payload with model ID, checkpoint ID, geometry token, flow velocity, sequence, local time/cycle tag, and validity bits.
Assert model_req_ready and model_req_valid appropriately for request issuance handshake.
Compare model_rsp_seq to outstanding sequence and compare model_rsp_timestamp or age to freshness threshold.
Verify presence of drag_force, lift_force, surface_pressure, and flow_field on every accepted response.
Set envelope_violation, stale_or_mismatched_response, response_invalid, unsupported_format, safe_fallback_active, and clamp_event conditions as appropriate.
Generate actuator_cmd from either validated model intent or safe fallback command and clamp/rate-limit each field.
Expose fault_status and saturating debug counters.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, all request tracking, outstanding sequence tracking, freshness and timeout age counters, fault flags, fallback latches, clamp flags, actuator outputs, and diagnostic counters reset to safe defaults. No request may be issued and no actuator command may be asserted until configuration is latched and input validation passes.
behavior_rules: If geometry_valid and flow_valid are asserted, geometry_format matches cfg_supported_geometry_format, and flow_velocity_mps lies within 20..55 inclusive, a request may be issued when no request is outstanding.
If the design is in fault-latched fallback, request issuance is inhibited until the fault condition clears according to the freshness and validation rules.
The request sequence counter increments on each accepted request and the sequence value is embedded in the outgoing payload.
A response is accepted only if model_rsp_valid is asserted, the sequence matches the outstanding sequence, the age is within freshness threshold, and all required fields are present.
A mismatched or stale response is rejected without affecting actuator outputs and increments rejected-response diagnostics.
Validated response data may be mapped into command intent only through a deterministic control_gain or intent_map_sel path; no continuous physics computation is performed.
Clamp and rate limiting apply to every actuator command field independently.
safe_fallback_active remains asserted until a fresh, sequence-matched, valid response is received and all fault conditions clear.
When fallback is active, actuator_cmd shall be the configured safe fallback command after clamping.
Diagnostic counters are saturating unsigned counters.
